q: A rolling boil sterilises the wort, drives off raw grain volatiles and coagulates protein out of solution. Which further job depends on that same heat?
opts: Generating the carbon dioxide that carbonates the beer
exp: Alpha acids are barely soluble until heat rearranges them, so a long boil is what actually extracts bitterness. Starch conversion has already finished in the mash, and the alcohol arrives later with the yeast.

q: Hops go into a ninety-minute boil at two moments, a charge at the start and another in the final few minutes. What does the late charge give that the early one cannot?
opts: Bitterness, because alpha acids need only brief contact
exp: The volatile oils that carry hop aroma survive a few minutes of heat but boil away over an hour, so bitterness and aroma need separate additions. It is why a beer can be intensely fragrant and only moderately bitter, or bracingly bitter and almost silent on the nose.

q: An IPA smells overwhelmingly of grapefruit, mango and pine yet drinks no more bitter than its recipe would suggest. Which cold addition, made well after the kettle, produced that nose?
exp: With no heat there is no isomerisation, so the oils are extracted while the bitterness is not. This is the technique behind the whole modern aromatic IPA family, and the aroma it gives fades with age faster than bitterness does.

q: Rice and maize turn up in the grist of a great many pale lagers around the world. What are they contributing?
opts: The husk that forms the filter bed
Fermentable sugar with very little flavour
The enzymes that convert the starch
exp: Adjuncts ferment out almost completely and leave next to no flavour behind, lightening body and colour and lowering cost as they go. A beer brewed to the Reinheitsgebot cannot use them, so the difference between the two is stylistic and not only legal.

q: One tank is held at twenty degrees Celsius and another at ten, each pitched with a different species of yeast. Which pair of words names the two families that result?
exp: Warm fermentation throws fruity esters and finishes in days; cold fermentation is slow and leaves a cleaner beer in which malt and hops speak plainly. Almost everything else that divides the two families follows from that one choice.

q: Fruity notes of banana, pear drop and apple appear in a warm-fermented beer that never had fruit anywhere near it. Which compounds are responsible?
exp: Esters are yeast by-products and they climb as fermentation temperature climbs, which is precisely why lager brewers keep their tanks cold. A Bavarian wheat beer is the extreme case, where one ester is deliberately encouraged rather than suppressed.

q: A lager tastes of butterscotch and coats the mouth slickly, and the brewer admits the tank was chilled down early. Which compound was never cleaned up?
exp: Yeast makes diacetyl during fermentation and reabsorbs it afterwards if left warm long enough, a step brewers call the diacetyl rest. Acetaldehyde is the green apple fault and comes from the same impatience.

q: A fine sediment sits in the bottom of the bottle, and the beer carbonated itself in the package rather than in a tank. Which practice produced that?
opts: Forced carbonation from a gas cylinder
exp: Live yeast and a small sugar addition ferment inside the sealed bottle, so the beer keeps developing and rewards a careful pour. Most Trappist beers and a great many Belgian ales arrive this way.

q: A British cellar holds an unfiltered, unpasteurised beer still working on its own yeast, drawn upstairs by a hand pump with no gas behind it. What is that beer called?
exp: Cask ale is served at cellar temperature with gentle natural carbonation, and once broached it has only a few days of useful life. Keg beer is filtered, sealed and pushed by gas, which is why it survives far longer on tap.

q: Weeks or months of near-freezing storage after the main fermentation drop out haze and round off the harshness of a young beer. What is that period called?
exp: Lagern is simply German for to store, and the whole family of beers took its name from the practice. The long cold rest is also when residual diacetyl and sulphur compounds are scrubbed away.

q: Copies of one 1842 original are sold all over the world under shortenings of its town's name. Which beer are all of them reaching back to?
opts: The pale golden lager of Plzen
exp: Soft Bohemian water, pale malt and Saaz hops gave a clear golden beer at the moment glassware became cheap enough for drinkers to see it. Nearly every industrial lager brewed since is a descendant of it.

q: Munich answered Bohemia with a pale lager of its own, rounder, softer in bitterness and leaning on bready malt. What is it called?
exp: Helles simply means pale, and the contrast with a Czech pilsner is malt-led balance against hop-led snap. Dunkel is the older dark Munich style that helles went on to displace at home, since what Spaten was answering in 1894 was the success of Bohemian pilsner.

q: An amber, toasty lager worked out by Anton Dreher in the 1840s took firmer root in Mexico than it ever did at home. Which style?
exp: Vienna malt gives the colour and a light toast without any roast bitterness behind it. Austrian brewers largely abandoned the style, while Austrian emigrants to Mexico kept it alive and it became a fixture there.

q: Bavarian brewing was forbidden over the hot months, so a stronger batch was laid down in one particular month and stored to last until autumn. Which style still carries that month in its name?
exp: Marzen means March, and whatever survived the summer was drunk off at the autumn festival, which is how it became the Oktoberfest beer. Modern festival beers are often paler and lighter than the classic amber version.

q: Monks in Munich brewed a strong dark lager to carry them through a fasting Lent, and its descendants almost all bear names ending in -ator. Which style is that?
exp: Liquid bread was the idea: heavy in malt, sweetish and generally seven to nine percent. Bock is the strong lager family and doppelbock its stronger branch, the suffix following the original Salvator.

q: A jet-black German lager reaches the table and the guest braces for something heavy and sweet, but it is dry, clean and light in body. Which style is in the glass?
exp: Colour and body are not the same property: a small quantity of dark malt colours a beer completely without adding weight to it. That is one of the most useful facts a server has when a guest announces they dislike dark beer.
